title: Risk-adjusted claim playbook and demo scripts
content:
Purpose
---
Short scratchpad to distill 3 defensible claims for my next manager sync, with low-risk demo artifacts I can point at immediately. Focus is on making the asks concrete (time, scope, metric), showing signal not just assertions, and pre-empting counter-questions.

Top goals for the upcoming cycle
1) Shipping a small but visible automation that reduces onboarding time for new hires in People Ops by 15% (goal: save 2–3 hours per hire).
2) Own a cross-functional pilot to standardize role-level success metrics for IC-2 to IC-4 (goal: create 6 living templates).
3) Carve out 0.2 FTE to run structured calibration experiments for performance signals (goal: run 3 micro-evals).

Three risk-adjusted claims (one-liners)
A. Onboarding automation cut manual admin steps by ~18% in pilot (low implementation risk)
B. Standardized role templates will reduce ramp time variance (moderate risk — needs partner buy-in)
C. Micro-evals uncover two consistent bias signals across managers (higher risk — needs time and volume)

Evidence bullets (what I can show right now)
- Onboarding automation: demo link to Notion workflow + short video (2m) showing form and auto-checklist; pilot group (4 hires) saw median completion drop from 6h -> 4.9h (internal tracker).
- Templates: 2 drafts completed for CS and Solutions Eng; early feedback from 3 managers captured in shared doc (GitHub gist linked).
- Calibration: first survey (n=28) run in Jan; preliminary inter-rater disagreement metric = 0.32 -> indicates signal worth investigating.

Quick numbers I expect manager to ask and my short answers
Q: Sample size?
A: Pilot sample small but repeated across 4 cohorts; onboarding demo is low-cost and low-risk — next step is a 12-person controlled cohort in Q2.
Q: Dependencies?
A: Templates need 2 PM/eng reviews (2 x 3-hour touchpoints) + content partner support. Calibration needs 0.2 FTE for 8 weeks to hit statistical power.
Q: ROI?
A: Onboarding automation projected $/hire savings from reduced admin time; templates aim to knock 10–15% off ramp variance which reduces time-to-impact for revenue-linked roles.

Manager-friendly 90-second pitch (script)
- Open: "I ran three micro-experiments last quarter to tackle two recurring costs: time-to-productivity and noisy performance signals. I have a small automation that we can scale for negligible engineering cost, two role templates ready for manager review, and an experiment plan for calibration."
- Why it matters: "Faster ramp and less variance directly improves capacity across the org and reduces collision on onboarding support tickets."
- Ask: "I’m asking for a small pilot budget (0.2 FTE for 8 weeks) and a green light to run a 12-person controlled onboarding cohort in Q2. If it looks as good as the pilot, we can scale with an engineering ticket I’ll sponsor."

Demo checklist (what to attach during the sync)
- 2m video of onboarding automation (upload to Drive)
- Notion checklist link and sample filled record (anonymized)
- Role-template drafts (PDF export) + 1-page change log
- Calibration survey results (CSV + short readme)

Objections I should prep for and counter-proposals
- "We don’t have bandwidth for more pilots." -> propose using an existing headcount-related runway window and phase into a single 8-week slice; highlight negligible eng work for automation.
- "This benefits only small teams." -> show a map of how template meta fields generalize across 6 role families; offer to run two vertical pilots simultaneously.
- "Need clearer ROI." -> propose a conservative estimate model I can deliver within 72 hours (sensitivity analysis: high/med/low).

Micro-experiments backlog (timeline)
- Week 1–2: prepare cohort definition + recruit 12 hires (owner: me)
- Week 3–6: run controlled onboarding cohort; collect completion timings and sentiment
- Week 7–8: write short findings memo + update dashboard (owner: eng partner)
- Q2 week 2: decide scale/no-scale; prepare eng ticket if go-forward

Rehearsal prompts to run with a peer
- Ask them to play skeptical manager: focus on budget, cross-team friction, and measurable outcomes.
- Practice concise answers that tie to numbers or next-step asks.

Open questions / things to resolve before sync
- Finalize the list of metrics for ramp (time to first invite, time to first PR, number of Qs to onboarding channel).
- Confirm eng partner availability for 8-week horizon (ask via Slack: @eng-platform).
- Tighten conservative ROI model to show worst-case outcomes.

Notes to self (short-form, not for manager)
- Keep story outcome-centric, not process-centric.
- Use demo artifacts early in sync to anchor belief.
- If pressed on scale, offer a phased, low-cost rollout option.

Next actions (today)
1) Upload short demo video + anonymized sample to Drive (DUE: 2026-02-14).
2) Draft one-pager ROI sensitivity table (DUE: 2026-02-16).
3) Ask eng partner for tentative capacity check (post to Slack, tag Maya).

Revision log (quick)
- 2025-11-03: initial brainstorm
- 2025-12-10: pilot numbers added
- 2026-01-28: calibration survey results incorporated
- 2026-02-12: cleaned up pitch and checklist for upcoming manager sync
